paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
model_annotation: The donut chart illustrates the distribution of samples (%) across combinations of two sample-level ambiguity metrics: Ambiguity Standard Deviation (outer ring) and Maximum Ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer),” is divided into four segments corresponding to standard deviation values of 0.0 (darkest blue, 49.0%), 0.47 (medium-dark blue, 47.7%), 0.82 (medium-light blue, 7.0%), and 0.94 (lightest blue, 5.0%). The inner ring, labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner),” is divided into three segments representing maximum ambiguity values of 1 (light blue, 38.0%), 2 (medium blue, 39.0%), and 3 (very light blue, 14.2%). Percentages are displayed directly on the chart segments, and a legend on the right clarifies the color coding for both metrics. The chart visually encodes the joint distribution of these two ambiguity measures across the dataset, with the outer ring segments summing to 100% and the inner ring segments also summing to 100%, indicating that each ring represents a separate marginal distribution rather than a nested or conditional one.
